newsitem.title: USA: Georgia FY98 budget includes $508 million of bonds.
newsitem.headline: Georgia FY98 budget includes $508 million of bonds.

text.p: Georgia Gov. Zell Miller presented state lawmakers with a proposed $11.778 million budget for fiscal 1998 that includes $508 million in bonds.
The budget for the year beginning July 1, 1997, increases spending by 4.6 percent over this year, Miller said.

The governor's budget report said appropriations would be funded from $11.118 billion in taxes and fees, $510 million in lottery proceeds, $148.8 million from the Indigent Care Trust Fund and $750,000 from anti-fraud levies.
Miller told lawmakers that state revenues would projected to grow at 4.6 percent for fiscal 1998.

"This is after we have set aside $152 million to account for the reduction of the sales tax on groceries by the third one-percent in October 1997 and after we have allowed for all of our reserves to be full on June 30, 1998," he said.
Miller's bond package includes:
--$98 million for local school construction
--$126.3 million in bonds for 20 capital outlay projects throughout the state university system and two other projects at facilities operated by the Board of Regents
--$110 million in bonds to continue funding the Governor's Road Improvement Program
--$28 million in bonds for seaports.
--$19.4 million in bonds for the Children and Youth Services department, including $14.2 million to build a new 150-bed Youth Development Campus in Sumter County

--$3.93 million in bonds to continue expansion of state crime laboratories, including $3.285 to build a new laboratory to replace the Columbus Branch Crime Lab and $645,000 to build a new facility for the first medical examiner facilities in Middle Georgia
--$10 million to acquire additional land under the RiverCare 2000 program
--$10.5 million for planning and design of the fourth phase of the World Congress Center
Miller told reporters he had designed the 1998 budget with a look to the future.
"I have built this budget carefully looking at what fiscal year 1999 would look like," he said. "I want to leave this state in good shape for the next governor."
He said the state had $550 million in reserves, including rainy day and lottery reserve funds.
"I'm always aware what our bond ratings are," Miller said. "I've looked at the out years. FY 99 will be tight. This year is tight, but we'll be able to do it."
Miller hinted the bond issue for World Congress Center might run into "trouble" with state lawmakers.
--Miami Bureau, 305-374-5013
